name: Benchmarking Synthetic Tabular Data
description: Evaluating the quality of synthetic data remains a key challenge for ensuring privacy and utility in data-driven research. In this work, we present an evaluation framework that quantifies how well synthetic data replicates original distributional properties while ensuring privacy. The proposed approach employs a holdout-based benchmarking strategy that facilitates quantitative assessment through low- and high-dimensional distribution comparisons, embedding-based similarity measures, and nearest-neighbor distance metrics. The framework supports various data types and structures, including sequential and contextual information, and enables interpretable quality diagnostics through a set of standardized metrics. These contributions aim to support reproducibility and methodological consistency in benchmarking of synthetic data generation techniques. The code of the framework is available at https://github.com/mostly-ai/mostlyai-qa.
reputation: Well-regarded within synthetic-data and privacy communities as a principled framework for benchmarking but not yet a universal standard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on tabular data; results are sensitive to choice of distance metrics and embedding models; risk of contamination if synthetic generators were trained on evaluation holdouts; benchmarks combine multiple heterogeneous metrics rather than a single scalar.
